plan.estimand: Omnibus F-test effect size (eta-squared = 0.06) in one-way ANOVA with 3 groups
plan.hypothesis: H0: All group means are equal vs. H1: At least one group mean differs
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size per group
Independent observations within and between groups
Normality: responses within each group are normally distributed
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance across all groups
Fixed effects model: groups are the only treatment factor
scientific_notes: Eta-squared is the population effect size (proportion of total variance explained by group membership)
The omnibus F-test is one-tailed in the upper tail of the F distribution under the alternative hypothesis
Minimum sample size is determined by inversion of the power function to achieve target power = 0.80
Integer rounding: report the smallest integer n per group that achieves or exceeds 80% power

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with k=3 independent normal groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.06, the minimum integer sample size per group that achieves at least 80% power for the omnibus F-test at α=0.05 is 52 participants per group (156 total). This design achieves 80.56% power, while the preceding design (n=51) achieves 79.73% power, confirming 52 as the smallest admissible design.
answer.method: Inverse power calculation using pwr::pwr.anova.test. Effect size converted from population eta-squared (0.06) to Cohen's f = 0.2526 via f = √(η²/(1−η²)). Minimum sample size identified by continuous solution (51.33) rounded up to nearest integer. Achieved power verified at selected design and preceding design.
assumptions: Balanced design with equal sample size per group
Independent observations within and between groups
Normality: responses within each group are normally distributed
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance across all groups
Omnibus F-test for equality of group means (upper-tail alternative)
limitations: Analysis assumes no missing data or dropout; no attrition inflation applied
Non-centrality parameter based on stated population eta-squared; actual effect sizes in preliminary data or prior studies should be confirmed
Design assumes standard ANOVA assumptions hold in practice
Sample size calculated for omnibus F-test only; post-hoc or planned comparisons may require additional sample size

executions.code:
# Install and load necessary package
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06           # population eta-squared (effect size)
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.80     # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
f <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))

cat("Effect size conversion:\n")
cat("Eta-squared:", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Cohen's f:", f, "\n\n")

# Calculate minimum sample size per group
# pwr.anova.test returns n = sample size per group
sample_size_result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

cat("Power analysis result:\n")
print(sample_size_result)

# Extract the continuous sample size solution
n_continuous <- sample_size_result$n
cat("\nContinuous solution: n =", n_continuous, "participants per group\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
n_integer <- ceiling(n_continuous)
cat("Rounded up (integer): n =", n_integer, "participants per group\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at n_integer
power_at_n_integer <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_integer,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", power_at_n_integer, "\n")

# Check power at the preceding integer (n_integer - 1)
power_at_n_minus_1 <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_integer - 1,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer - 1, ":", power_at_n_minus_1, "\n\n")

# Summary output
cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group: ", n_integer, "\n")
cat("Total participants (k=3 groups): ", k * n_integer, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", round(power_at_n_integer, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_integer - 1, "):", round(power_at_n_minus_1, 6), "\n")

# Return result for structured reporting
result_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "total_participants", value = k * n_integer, unit = "count"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_n_integer, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(f, 6), unit = "effect_size")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\nJSON Output:\n")
cat(result_json)
